full_judgment:
2. On 8-8-85 the plaintiff M/s Bangladesh Electrical Company Ltd. PS Tongi, Dist. Gazipur instituted the suit for declaration of his right, title and interest in the two industrial plots of land, namely, plot Nos. A-102 and A-103 situated within the Bangladesh Small & Cottage Industries Corporation's Industrial Estate, Tongi, District Gazipur, against 8 persons viz M/s Shafi Textile Ltd. of Bangladesh Small and Cottage Industrial. Estate Tongi police station; the Deputy Manager, BSCIC Industrial, Estate Tongi, Police Station Tongi District Gazipur; the Deputy Commissioner, District Gazipur; the Officer-in-Charge, Tongi Police Station, District Gazipur, as defendant Nos.1, 4, 6 and 7 respectively and also 3 officials of BSCIC, Head Office at Motijheel, Dhaka as defendant Nos. 2, 3 and 5 and the Secretary, Ministry of Industries, Govt. of Bangladesh Shilpa Bhaban, Dhaka as Defendant No. 8. 

 3. Plaintiffs's case, as it appears from the original plaint, in short, is that by a letter of allotment No. IE. Tongi-P/64/68/737(3) dated 6-5-68, issued by the then Small Cottage Industries Corporation, he got the plot Nos. A-102 and A-103 of BSCIC Industrial Estate, Tongi, in the District of formerly Dhaka, at present Gazipur, on perpetual lease for setting up an Industry for manufacturing Electric Cable and other accessories. Upon execution of the required lease deed and taking over possession therein, he constructed buildings and boundary wall thereon and also set up machineries therein, spending Taka 15 lakh for construction works and Taka 10 lakh for the machineries. During liberation war in Bangladesh the aforesaid buildings were severely damaged and machinery parts were looted away. 

 5. It is alleged that some influential officials of Bangladesh Small Cottage Industries Corporation, herein after referred to as "BSCIC", to favour the defendant No. 1 M/s Shafi Textiles Ltd. with a plot of land in that industrial estate, had started a false proceeding against the plaintiff with a view to cancelling his allotment of those plots of land and ultimately, the land allotment committee of the BSCIC Industrial Estate Tongi, in its meeting, held on 14-11-84, illegally cancelled the allotment of plot No. A-103 without showing any reasonable cause, notwithstanding the fact that he has, regularly, been paying the instalment money as well as the rent. The defendant Nos. 2-5 have no legal right to cancel such allotment of the suit land to the plaintiff. Defendant No. 1 had managed through the defendant Nos. 2-5 to cancel the said allotment made in favour of the plaintiff with regard to the aforesaid plot No. A-103. The defendant No. 1 has been trying to enter into the said plot No. A-103. He has also influenced the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 for creating disturbance in the peaceful enjoyment of the industrial concern of the plaintiff. Accordingly, in paragraph 7 of the plaint of the plaintiff, stated that the cause of action of the suit arose on 24-12-84, then on 24-6-85 and on 6-7-85 and lastly, on 27-7-85 and still it has been continuing within the jurisdiction of the court under Police Station Motijheel, District Dhaka. 

 6. The plaintiff prayed for the following reliefs in the suit: (a) To pass a decree declaring the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in the schedule allotted plots bearing plot No. A-102 and plot No. A-103 BSCIC Industrial Estate, Tongi against the defendants (b) To pass a decree for costs against the defendants (c) To pass a decree granting any other relief or reliefs to which this plaintiff is entitled under law, equity and justice. 

 "District Gazipur, under Sadar Sub-Registry, Police Station Tongi, BSCIC Industrial plot Nos. 1-102 and A-103 BSCIC Industrial Estate Tongi, Gazipur having industrial concern in the name and style of Bangladesh Electrical Company Limited". 

 "6(a) That the added defendant No. 9 is a stranger and during the lis pendens of this suit forcibly entered into some parts of the scheduled property in plot No. A-103 without any lawful authority and therefore, the added defendant has got no right, title, interest in leasehold property of this plaintiff and the illegal forcible entry in the schedule property is needed to be removed by the defendant Nos. 2-6. More particularly, the defendant No. 4 is legally bound to withdraw the added defendant No. 9 from the scheduled property, which is the exclusive lease-hold property of the plaintiff" 

 16. In such view of the matter submission of Mr. Nurul Hoque that the cause of action of the suit arose at Motijheel, Dhaka as soon as the letters cancelling his allotment to industrial Plot No. A-103 were issued from the Dhaka Office of BSCIC cannot be accepted.
